note: Two hazards, both learned the hard way this session. FIRST: never put backticks in a board NOTE. They survive into a shell context as command substitution. A NOTE of mine quoting the phrase make-rebaseline in backticks ACTUALLY RAN make rebaseline, which aborted at schema-backfill, wrote a spurious row into docs/timings.md and left an orphaned zero-byte schema.json.tmp under book/src/laboratory/generated/the-census/. Swept both; committed artifacts diffed clean and HEAD was untouched. This is the same family as the documented PATHS-vs-FIELDS quoting trap, so treat a NOTE as shell-adjacent text: no backticks, no dollar-parens. SECOND: the census opt-in guard is a substring match on the COMMAND TEXT, not on intent. A git commit whose MESSAGE merely names the opt-in variable assignment is refused with the same error a real census attempt gets. Write it as the canonical-host-only census env var in commit messages, ledgers and dispatch prompts. Do NOT reach for the AUTHORIZED escape hatch to get a commit through: it asserts the owner authorized a census run, which is a carve-out, and a commit message is never a reason to claim one. THIRD, related: adding ANY registry metric grows the registry-derived census schema while committed rows.csv fixtures keep the old column count, so the nine metrics-all studies stop reconstructing and the lab calibration tests go red. 43 here, 42 at the precedent commit 71ed4eeb whose message documents the same deliberate red. rebaseline exits non-zero at schema-backfill and takes four later steps with it; run those by hand. What makes it safe rather than reckless: classify EVERY failure programmatically with grep -c on the string rows.csv-header-does-not-match-study and require that count to EQUAL the failure count. 43 of 43 here. If even one failure lacks the signature, it is yours, not the fixtures.
